dz.headline: Algerians vote for local councils as 162,864 candidates compete
dz.dek: The ballot selects members of municipal and provincial assemblies across 1,541 communes and 69 wilayas for five-year terms.
paragraphs: More than 24 million Algerians were called to vote on Saturday for members of municipal and provincial assemblies, with polling stations opening at 08:00. The vote covers 1,541 communes and 69 wilayas, and the representatives will serve five-year terms.

A total of 162,864 candidates are contesting the seats on 6,065 lists, according to the National Independent Electoral Authority. Of the candidates, 141,388 are running for municipal assemblies and 21,476 for provincial assemblies. The councils oversee local concerns including roads, schools, street lighting, waste collection, transport and urban planning.

The campaign ended at midnight on Tuesday. Candidates largely focused on local development and daily concerns; some used artificial intelligence to make campaign materials, which sometimes included errors in names and images.

dz.headline: Algeria plans tighter well controls as El Menia groundwater falls
dz.dek: The agriculture minister says farm expansion must match local water supplies and plans wider use of efficient irrigation and treated wastewater.
paragraphs: A lawmaker from El Menia, in southern Algeria, has warned that groundwater levels are falling, raising concern about the future of farms as agriculture expands. Abdelhamid Belkhel made the warning to the agriculture minister at the National People’s Assembly, but gave no figure for the decline.

Belkhel said investors could leave their farms and abandon dry land if groundwater reserves continue to shrink. The minister said cultivated areas must reflect each territory’s water capacity, rather than expand without limit.

The agriculture sector plans tighter oversight of drilling permits, wider use of water-saving irrigation and greater use of treated wastewater, in coordination with other departments. Belkhel also called for developing vegetable production in El Menia, which faces difficulties supplying vegetables.

dz.headline: Air Algérie offers up to 50% off winter flights to Algeria
dz.dek: The discount covers travel from 26 November through 31 January, with bookings open until 3 December.
paragraphs: Air Algérie, the national airline, is offering discounts of up to 50% on flights from abroad to Algeria for winter travel, it said on 27 November. The offer applies to trips from 26 November 2026 through 31 January 2027.

Travellers must book by 3 December to use the promotion, which overlaps with winter school holidays in France beginning on 18 December. TSA Algerie reported that the period usually brings higher demand for flights between France and Algeria, where rising ticket prices have drawn criticism from members of the Algerian diaspora.
The airline said the sale began on 26 November. Air Algérie has also received its fourth Boeing 737 MAX 8, a jet model from the US manufacturer Boeing, TSA Algerie reported.

dz.headline: Algerian gendarmes dismantle armed drug network across five wilayas
dz.dek: Authorities arrested 31 suspects and seized cocaine, cannabis, more than one million psychotropic pills and weapons in the two-week operation.
paragraphs: Algeria’s National Gendarmerie dismantled an armed network trafficking drugs and psychotropic substances across Béjaïa, Batna, Sétif, Bouira and Algiers during an operation lasting two weeks, the Defence Ministry said on Friday, 27 November. The operation led to 31 arrests.

The ministry said investigators seized 160 kilograms of cocaine, 150 kilograms of processed cannabis and more than one million Pregabalin pills. They also recovered 44 passenger and utility vehicles, seven motorcycles, a jet ski, two automatic pistols and a shotgun. The suspects were brought before the competent judicial authorities.

The ministry said a related money-laundering network transferred $1.98 million in criminal proceeds from drug trafficking to the United Arab Emirates. Investigators also recovered cash in Algerian and Tunisian currency, euros and counterfeit banknotes.

dz.headline: Timimoun hosts Polish delegation for talks on farm investment
dz.dek: The visitors examined prospects for investment in strategic crops and partnerships with Algerian operators at the Tinerkouk El-Kebir farm area.
paragraphs: A high-level Polish delegation visited the Tinerkouk El-Kebir agricultural area in Timimoun province on Wednesday 25 November to examine farming opportunities, Algeria’s local agricultural services directorate said. The visit was organised on the agriculture minister’s instruction with local authorities and the head of the office for developing industrial agriculture on Saharan land.

Local agriculture officials, representatives of the agriculture chamber and investors from the province received the delegation. Discussions covered investment in strategic crops, technical expertise-sharing and possible direct or joint ventures between Algerian and Polish economic operators, the directorate said.
The visit follows an Italian partnership led by Bonifiche Ferraresi for durum wheat, cereals, pulses and food processing in Timimoun.

ao.headline: FAO and WFP warn of worsening food insecurity risk in Angola
ao.dek: The agencies cite drought, expected cereal-production declines and the risk of a late start to the next rainy season.
paragraphs: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) warned in a Hunger Hotspots report presented on Friday that acute food insecurity in Angola faces a credible risk of worsening. The agencies said the country lacked updated data for a comparative assessment using their agreed method.

They said rainfall deficits during the 2025/26 farming season are expected to reduce output in central provinces, Angola’s main cereal-producing areas, and in the east. Repeated droughts have limited food availability in the south and west for years and weakened livelihoods and households’ ability to respond, the report said.

Recovery is expected to remain slow, with forecasts pointing to a risk of a late start to the next rainy season in the south and west, linked to El Niño conditions. Cereals are usually harvested from April to June.

ao.headline: Bosch expands Angola range and plans local engineering department
ao.dek: The German company will add appliances, auto parts and industrial equipment, and is targeting manufacturing, mining, oil and gas, and agriculture.
paragraphs: Bosch is expanding beyond power tools in Angola, adding appliances, automotive parts, industrial boilers, automation and industrial hydraulics. The German multinational selected Angola as one of three early markets for its One Bosch strategy, which brings its business lines under one presence in each market.

Maurilio Carbonel Mateus, Bosch Angola’s director-general for business, strategy and marketing, said the company is investing in local staff training and plans an engineering department for technical support and project work. Bosch said its market share rose from about 16% to 31% in four years, while its distribution network now reaches 10 of Angola’s 21 provinces.

The expanded range is aimed at manufacturing, food processing, mining, oil and gas, and agriculture. Bosch opened a representative office in Angola in 2015 and built local storage, after-sales service and customer relations capabilities from 2018 to 2025.

ao.headline: Angola's geological institute targets five mineral areas for assessment
ao.dek: The proposed 12-to-24-month plan would rank priority sites among approximately 3,000 mineral occurrences identified across the country.
paragraphs: Angola’s Geological Institute (IGEO) has identified approximately 3,000 mineral occurrences across the country and proposed choosing about five priority areas for prospecting and mining investment. Administrator Américo da Mata presented the plan in Luanda on Thursday, 26 November, at the Angola International Mining Conference.

The proposed work would take 12 to 24 months and involve IGEO and the National Mineral Resources Agency (ANRM), da Mata said. The institute would rank the areas, while ANRM would promote identified opportunities to potential investors. Companies interested in a site would then need to conduct detailed geological surveys, geochemical analyses and drilling to assess and classify resources.

IGEO’s publicly accessible geological information includes mineral types and their locations. Da Mata cautioned that identifying an occurrence does not establish that it is an economically viable reserve; further studies must determine its size, quality and economic viability.

ao.headline: BODIVA shares slip 1% to 99,001 kwanzas on Thursday
ao.dek: The Angolan stock exchange operator's shares closed at 99,001 kwanzas after 77 shares changed hands in a small correction on the secondary market.
paragraphs: Shares in the Bolsa de Dívida e Valores de Angola (BODIVA), the body that runs Angola's debt and securities market, closed Thursday's session at 99,001 kwanzas, down from 100,000 kwanzas at the previous close. That is a fall of about 1%.
During the session 77 of the institution's shares were traded, a movement the outlet describes as a slight correction in the stock's price on the secondary market.

The fall comes as Angola's capital market works to consolidate its growth by drawing in more investors and widening the financial instruments available for trade. The outlet says the movement in BODIVA's price is worth watching, given the institution's role in organising, managing and developing the market.

ao.headline: Angolan banker named among 50 influential mining leaders
ao.dek: António Dinis Mendes was recognised in Luanda for linking finance with mining as his bank plans export pre-financing, equipment loans and supplier guarantees.
paragraphs: António Dinis Mendes, chief executive of the African Bank of Oman (ABO), was named one of Angola’s 50 most influential mining leaders at a ceremony in Luanda on 24 November. The recognition was organised by ETOSSI Mining Angola for his work connecting finance and mining investment.

Mendes said banks should develop finance for different project stages, from exploration to production, and share risks with other banks and multilateral institutions. ABO plans to offer mining companies export pre-financing, equipment finance and guarantees for suppliers, alongside international trade services.

The bank also plans partnerships to support larger projects and wants to connect Angolan mining opportunities with investors in the Middle East. Mendes said those investors are increasingly interested in diversifying in Africa and take a long-term view.

bj.headline: Benin's social security fund moves employer filings and payments online
bj.dek: From 1 December, employers must use the national public-services portal for registration certificates and social-contribution payments.
paragraphs: Benin’s National Social Security Fund will require employers to submit applications for registration certificates and pay social contributions through the national public-services portal from 1 December 2026. The fund announced the change in a statement on 27 November.

The new rule ends in-person submission of those applications at the fund’s agencies. Employers needing a registration certificate or paying contributions must send their files and complete payments online, the fund said.
The fund urged employers to prepare for the change before it takes effect. The requirement covers all employers seeking the certificates or settling social contributions.

bj.headline: EU allocates 350 000 euros for displaced people in northern Benin
bj.dek: The extra funding targets people uprooted by violence and hunger, with the money earmarked for disaster preparation, protection, health and nutrition services.
paragraphs: The European Union announced an additional 350 000 euros on 27 November for people displaced in northern Benin, saying the money would support those affected by violence, flight from their villages and hunger.

The EU said the funding would strengthen disaster preparation and protection, health and nutrition services. The government counts more than 34 000 refugees and asylum seekers in Benin, in addition to people displaced inside the country.
The four northern departments covered by the Programme for Northern Benin (PRONORD), which runs from 2024 to 2029 with 33,75 million euros, are Alibori, Atacora, Borgou and Donga.

bj.headline: Benin's economic council seeks 40.69% budget increase for 2027
bj.dek: The CFA5.295 billion request includes costs from the former Republic Mediator's duties, now folded into the council's remit.
paragraphs: Benin’s Economic and Social Council (CES) asked parliament’s finance and trade committee for CFA5.295 billion for 2027, a 40.69% increase on its 2026 budget of 3.764 billion. The council presented the proposal on Nov. 26, saying its expanded responsibilities include work previously handled by the Republic Mediator.

Pascal Essou, the CES’s second vice-president, presented the request on behalf of council president Abdoulaye Bio Tchané. The proposed funds cover staff, goods and services, and transfers. In 2026, the council adopted eight studies and continued four more, covering areas including agriculture, employment, health and mobility.
The CES also plans to review the 2028 budget guidance note and corresponding finance bill in 2027. Its 2027-2031 strategic plan sets out a framework for expanding its own-initiative studies.

bj.headline: Benin seeks CFA181,9 billion for farm investment and higher output
bj.dek: The proposed 2027 budget targets 724 281 tonnes of cotton, alongside higher cereal and soybean harvests.
paragraphs: Benin’s agriculture ministry is seeking CFA181,9 billion for its 2027 budget, including investment in farm equipment and higher production. The proposal, presented to the National Assembly’s budget committee on Thursday 26 November, sets a cotton target of 724 281 tonnes for the 2027-2028 season.

The request is up from CFA144,1 billion in the 2026 revised finance law. Of the proposed total, CFA123,1 billion would fund investment and CFA58,8 billion operations, while the ministry expects cereal output to reach 4,1 million tonnes and soybean production one million tonnes.

The ministry also plans supplementary irrigation for a thousand producers across 10 000 hectares and six industrial seed-production units. Funding would come 54% from domestic resources, 43% from borrowing and 3% from grants.

bw.headline: DStv reshapes five packages with lower prices and more channels
bw.dek: The Botswana offering adds dedicated sports and movies packages, while Starter now carries more than 85 channels.
paragraphs: DStv has launched five redesigned packages in Botswana, with reduced pricing and new channels, as part of its first full overhaul in 30 years. The packages let subscribers choose options built around interests such as sport, movies and series, rather than relying only on traditional tiers.

The company says DStv Starter now has more than 85 channels, including SuperSport KICKOFF and Wethu+, while DStv Select has more than 100. DStv Sports carries over 115 channels, and DStv Ultimate has more than 130. DStv Movies & Series is a separate offering for film and series viewers.

The new premium channels include Wethu+, M-Net Movies+, M-Net Stars and M-Net Legends. DStv says entry-level subscribers also gain access to content that was previously unavailable at those price points.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso restarts Perkoa mine after four years idle
bf.dek: The state mining company has resumed operations at the polymetallic site, closed since April 2022 after underground flooding killed eight workers.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso restarted operations at the Perkoa polymetallic mine on Friday, 27 November 2026, under state mining company SOPAMIB. The mine had been closed since April 2022, when flooding in its underground galleries killed eight workers.

SOPAMIB’s director general, Lamissa Barro, said the restart followed rehabilitation work begun in April 2026. Measures include clearing and widening a rainwater channel, rebuilding civil works, strengthening a protective dyke and installing 90 kW pumps. The company also plans water-level monitoring and video surveillance.
SOPAMIB created a wholly state-owned subsidiary, SOPAMIB Perkouan, to lead the process. Consultations with nearby communities began in March 2026.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger approve digital cooperation framework
bf.dek: The agreement covers connected networks, postal services and cybersecurity, with diplomatic review and leaders’ approval still ahead.
paragraphs: Ministers responsible for digital affairs and postal services in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger approved a draft cooperation framework in Ouagadougou on Friday, 27 November. The agreement covers digital services and postal cooperation among the three countries.

Burkina Faso’s digital transition minister, Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, said the framework and accompanying technical documents were approved after presentations and discussions. Its provisions include sharing and connecting digital infrastructure, securing cyberspace and developing cooperation protocols and detailed road maps.

The draft must now pass through the three foreign ministries before going to the countries’ leaders for approval and signature. Proposed projects include linking national communications networks, joint equipment and service purchases, and shared negotiations with international companies such as satellite internet provider Starlink.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso mini-dairies seek role in public milk initiatives
bf.dek: The network collected 1 838 849 litres of local milk and reported more than CFA1.3 billion in revenue in 2025.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso’s 12th Local Milk Days opened in Ouagadougou on Friday, 27 November 2026, with mini-dairies’ place in public initiatives as its theme. The three-day gathering, organised by the National Union of Mini-Dairies and Milk Producers of Burkina (UMPLB), is intended to bring industry participants together and identify solutions to local milk processors’ difficulties.

UMPLB president El Hadj Ibrahim Adama Diallo said the network wants mini-dairies recognised as partners in public policy. In 2024, it had 101 mini-dairies and 94 producer organisations, with about 4 000 members; nearly 80% were women and 35% were young people. Diallo said the dairies collected 1 838 849 litres of local milk in 2025 and generated more than CFA1.3 billion in revenue.

Since 2021, the network has organised vocational certificate training and introductions to green-sector jobs across seven trades. It has also helped establish 9 milk restaurants and develop the FaireFaso lait-local-équitable collective brand, registered with the African Intellectual Property Organization in December 2023.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso’s social security fund honours nine firms for workplace safety
bf.dek: The first national occupational health and safety prize recognised companies in mining, construction, industry and services at Kaya’s three-day event.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso’s National Social Security Fund (CNSS) honoured nine companies with its first National Occupational Health and Safety Prize in Kaya on Friday, 27 November. The awards closed the 16th edition of the fund’s three-day workplace risk-prevention event, which began on 25 November.

CNSS Director General Herman Yacouba Nacambo said the companies were selected after an evaluation and recognised across mining, construction and public works, industry, and services. More than 150 participants from different regions of Burkina Faso attended discussions on working conditions and quality of life at work.

Nacambo said the prize was created because workplace safety practices at some companies were little known and rarely shared. The event also produced recommendations on handling workplace conflict, training managers and expanding workplace health committees’ remit.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso opens Kadiogo fish fair to connect producers with urban buyers
bf.dek: The 26-28 November event in Koubri features fish sales, panels and business meetings for local producers and processors.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry is holding the first commercial and gastronomic fair for fish and fish products in Kadiogo from 26 to 28 November 2026 in Koubri. The event brings together exhibitions and sales, panel discussions, entertainment and business-to-business meetings.

The chamber says the fair is intended to promote local producers’ and processors’ skills and connect local supply with urban demand. Koubri’s special delegation president, Samadé Léonard Gougou, said the area has fish farming, fishing and fish processing activity. He cited agriculture ministry figures showing national fish production above 53 000 tonnes, against overall needs above 100 000 tonnes.
A representative of the chamber’s patron, Seydou Zanga Sessouma, said Kadiogo recorded 25 000 tonnes of fish consumption. The fair’s theme focuses on raising incomes in the fish sector.

bi.headline: Burundi's election commission rejects Rwasa's presidential bid
bi.dek: The commission says he failed to prove he had been outside party politics for at least a year, while his representative plans an appeal.
paragraphs: Burundi’s Independent National Electoral Commission rejected Agathon Rwasa’s bid for the presidency on 27 November in Bujumbura, saying he did not qualify to run as an independent. The presidential election is scheduled for 3 May 2027.

The commission rejected three of the 10 applications it reviewed and approved seven. Its president, Prosper Ntahorwamiye, said Rwasa submitted a statement that he had left party leadership bodies in 2024, rather than the required declaration that he had not claimed membership of any political party for at least one year. The commission also considers him a member of the National Congress for Liberty, the opposition party he formerly led.
Pamphile Malayika, Rwasa’s representative, called the decision scandalous and said he would appeal to the Constitutional Court.

bi.headline: Burundi communes face pressure to turn 22 billion FBu into youth jobs
bi.dek: The 2026-27 budget sets aside 22 billion FBu for each commune, while young people describe scarce work and limited prospects.
paragraphs: Burundi’s 2026-27 budget allocates more than 944 billion FBu to provinces and communes, including 22 billion FBu for each commune. The funds come as many young people struggle to find work, according to Yaga Burundi’s report.

People younger than 35 make up more than 70% of Burundi’s population of 12.33 million, based on the 2024 census. Jeanne Nakiteretse, social affairs adviser in Ntahangwa commune, said the commune gives many tax-collector jobs to young people, but some remain unemployed and further activities are planned.

Vianney Ndayisaba, national coordinator of the Association for the Fight Against Unemployment and Torture, urged communes to use state funds and tax revenue for local economic activity. At a September 23, 2026, planning debate in Gitega, Kiganda’s administrator Diane Kaneza said involving young people in project design remained a challenge.

bi.headline: Cholera infects at least 12 Saint-Marc students amid water shortage
bi.dek: The boarding school in Bujumbura has reportedly lacked potable water for nearly two weeks, while parents say students cannot return home.
paragraphs: At least 12 students at Lycée Saint-Marc, a boarding school in Bujumbura, have contracted cholera since Wednesday, SOS Médias Burundi reported. Students said the school had been without potable water for nearly two weeks and linked the shortage to the spread of the disease.

Seven students were taken to Prince Régent Charles Hospital on Wednesday, and five more were brought there on Thursday, according to the report. The school’s director confirmed cholera cases but declined to give further details. Students said their parents had not been informed; parents said the director would not allow students to return to their families.
Cases were also reported in Cibitoke and Bwiza, where eight people were said to be affected. Administrative authorities confirmed the reports but gave no further details.

paragraphs: Bonaventure Niyongabo, a senior cameraman at Burundi’s public media known as Gihuha, was released on Thursday evening, 26 November, after several days in detention at the National Intelligence Service in Bujumbura, SOS Médias Burundi reported.

cm.headline: Cameroon plans CFA50 billion more in annual beverage taxes
cm.dek: The 2027 finance bill would raise excise duties and add a CFA5 stamp duty to each bottled drink.
paragraphs: Cameroon’s 2027 finance bill proposes raising excise duties on bottled drinks and adding a CFA5 stamp duty to each bottle, with the government expecting CFA50 billion in extra tax revenue a year. The proposal covers brewers and makers of soft drinks and other bottled beverages.

The measures under discussion would increase costs by CFA100 to CFA150 per bottle, a rise of 10% to 20% depending on the brand, Journal du Cameroun reported. Producers say the state already receives 55% of a bottle’s price through taxes. The producers’ association says the industry provides 10 000 direct jobs and supports about 6 000 farmers and nearly 2 900 partner small businesses.

The proposal also comes after repeated increases in beverage duties since 2019 and rising energy, raw-material and freight costs, the report said. The government has previously blocked operators from raising prices, with the Commerce Ministry setting a CFA50 limit in 2019.

cm.headline: World Bank adds CFA36 billion for Cameroon rice irrigation
cm.dek: The extra $60 million will fund unfinished works in the Benoue Valley and extend the project deadline to June 30, 2029.
paragraphs: Cameroon will receive an extra $60 million, about CFA36 billion, from the World Bank to finish irrigation works in the Benoue Valley, in the North Region. Officials want the money to lift domestic rice output, boost farm incomes and cut the country's dependence on imported rice.

Money from the World Bank will cover unfinished infrastructure, shifts in construction costs and quantities, and safety upgrades to the Lagdo Dam, the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development said. The project now runs two years longer, to June 30, 2029, so works on 7,131 hectares of farmland can be completed.
The project began with a World Bank credit of roughly CFA117 billion. The extension was agreed on November 24 at steering committee meetings in Yaounde.

cm.headline: Cameroon identifies CFA4.1 trillion in potential investments
cm.dek: After its investment forum, the government says financing and project monitoring are now priorities, but gives no total for funds secured.
paragraphs: Cameroon identified more than CFA4.1 trillion in potential investments after the fifth Cameroon Investment Forum, held in Yaoundé from November 18 to 20. The 26 priority projects are valued at CFA3,928.3 billion, the Investment Promotion Agency said.

Boma Donatus, the agency’s acting director general, presented the figures at a November 26 press conference. The forum drew 78 proposals from government agencies, local authorities, private companies and independent developers; their estimated cost exceeds CFA6,862 billion, with more than CFA6,102 billion in financing required. The agency selected 43 projects it judged developed enough to present to potential investors.

Donatus said the government’s next priorities are securing financing, supporting project developers and setting up a monitoring system to move proposals toward implementation, job creation and expanded productive capacity.

cm.headline: Cameroon opens coffee organisation to consumer countries
cm.dek: A revised framework lets African coffee-consuming countries seek membership and join producers in discussions on processing, marketing and sales.
paragraphs: Cameroon signed an agreement in Yaounde opening the Inter-African Coffee Organization to African coffee-consuming countries, giving them a route to seek membership alongside producers. Trade Minister Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana signed the deal at the opening of the organisation’s 66th annual meetings.

The 2020 framework replaces the organisation’s 1998 rules and creates a platform for producers and consumers to discuss coffee processing, marketing and sales within Africa. Mbarga Atangana, the organisation’s outgoing president, said the continent’s 1.3 billion consumers offered producers and processors more buyers. He said stronger intra-African trade could reduce reliance on volatile international markets.

Cameroon’s local roasters processed about 750 tonnes in the 2024-25 season, nearly 7% more than the previous season, after a 44% decline, according to the National Cocoa and Coffee Board. The board recorded robusta prices of CFA1,300 to CFA2,500 per kilogram and arabica prices of CFA2,500 to CFA3,500.

cm.headline: MPEC seeks to unseat ruling party in Dja and Lobo’s five seats
cm.dek: Professor Jean-Calvin Aba’a Oyono leads a six-person slate challenging the ruling party’s hold on the department’s National Assembly seats.
paragraphs: Professor Jean-Calvin Aba’a Oyono has filed to contest Cameroon’s 2027 legislative elections in Dja and Lobo, leading a Mouvement populaire pour l’émergence du Cameroun (MPEC) slate seeking all five National Assembly seats held by the ruling Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais (RDPC). The list includes MPEC national president Martine Danielle Befolo Essono, Thomas Dydime Tomo Ze, Edjimbi Epse Nkoumou Nkoumsu and Jean Cyrille Abondo Ngono, as well as their respective substitutes. The Electoral Council must decide whether to accept the slate before the candidates can compete.

Aba’a Oyono was detained for a month after protests over the results of the 12 October 2025 presidential election, the report says. He later filed appeals against external intelligence services and Defence personnel.

cf.headline: Central African Republic creates committee to check food prices
cf.dek: The body will monitor market supply, social measures and transport costs as food and fuel prices rise across the country.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic government has created a joint committee to monitor prices and social measures, following rising food costs and transport fares across the country. Justice Minister Arnaud Djoubaye Abazène chaired a meeting in Bangui last Wednesday to set out the committee’s work.

Abazène said the committee, formed on the prime minister’s instructions, brings together government members, social partners and trade unions. Its commissions will check prices and market supplies, review administrative and pay reforms for civil servants, and track support for unions. Mixed inspection teams are to conduct unannounced checks, with union delegates observing.
The committee is also tasked with monitoring the removal of illegal road and river barriers. Government officials were due to report back to it the following week on their assigned work.

cf.headline: Central African Republic targets 6% of budget for health in 2027
cf.dek: Finance Minister Hervé Ndoba also pledged to raise the share from about 4% in 2026 to 10% by 2029, with quarterly reviews.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic plans to increase the share of its national budget for health to 6% in 2027, from about 4% in 2026. Finance Minister Hervé Ndoba announced the target on 25 November at the 5th International Conference on Public Health in Africa in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The government also set a 10% target for 2029 and will track budget execution every quarter, the announcement said. The reviews are intended to strengthen transparency and the effectiveness of public spending.

Ndoba outlined possible funding sources, including forest carbon credits from the Congo Basin, debt conversions into health-sector investment and pension funds. The conference ran from 23 to 27 November and was co-organised by Africa CDC and Ethiopia’s government.

cf.headline: Central African Republic collects far less from mining and forests than it could
cf.dek: World Bank-commissioned experts say enforcing the new mining code could double or triple state revenue from the two sectors.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic collects far less tax revenue from mining and forestry than those sectors could generate, according to experts commissioned by the World Bank. Enforcing the new mining code could double or triple public income from the two sectors, they said.

The World Bank's latest public-finance review found that public investment depends almost entirely on foreign aid, while civil-service salaries absorb a large share of available funds. The country has gold and diamonds underground and some of the largest forests in the Congo Basin, but taxes and royalties on resources leaving the country do not reliably reach the treasury.

Nearly three million people, about two-thirds of the population, live below the poverty line, and the country ranks 191st of 193 in the United Nations Human Development Index. Journalistic investigations and United Nations expert reports have described the involvement of companies linked to Russia's Wagner group in natural-resource extraction.

cf.headline: Central African Republic briefs lawmakers on national land policy
cf.dek: The urban-planning ministry and FAO held the 24 November workshop as part of a project to develop and implement the policy.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic’s urban-planning ministry and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) briefed lawmakers on 24 November on how the country’s national land policy is being developed. The workshop was part of a project supporting the policy’s preparation and implementation.

Emmanuel Christian Ouyamba, the ministry’s chief of staff, said lawmakers needed to understand land issues across agriculture, livestock and fishing. He said legal instruments on land were dispersed and that the policy process sought to bring them together to reduce the risk of conflict. FAO representative Labia Irène Ouaba reaffirmed the agency’s support for the government.
After the workshop, lawmakers were due to receive guidance on land governance and on validating future texts intended to improve it, Oubangui Medias reported.

cf.headline: Ngaragba prison tensions grow over informant claims and tramadol sales
cf.dek: A suspected inmate informant and repeated confinement in a cell have fuelled distrust among prisoners and disagreements between prison officials.
paragraphs: Tensions at Ngaragba Central Prison in Bangui have grown amid accusations between inmates, contested disciplinary sanctions and disagreements between the prison governor and head of security, Corbeau News Centrafrique reported on Friday. The report said an inmate had been held in a punishment cell several times, a case that has become a focus of the dispute.

The outlet said its investigation found that the governor allegedly used an unidentified prisoner to observe inmates, listen to their conversations and relay information. Other prisoners were not necessarily aware of the alleged arrangement. The report described conditions in the cell as particularly difficult but gave no dates for the confinements.
A suspected sale of tramadol, a medicine, triggered a fresh round of tensions, the outlet reported. It did not identify who was suspected of selling it or report any official response.

km.headline: Comoros official urges stronger voice in international negotiations
km.dek: At MEDays 2026 in Tangier, Nour El-Fath Azali said island states need stronger institutions, skills and political will to advance their interests.
paragraphs: Nour El-Fath Azali, Comoros’ secretary-general of government, called for the country to have more influence in international negotiations at MEDays 2026 in Tangier, Morocco. He spoke on a panel titled “From the periphery to the decision-making table.”

Azali said island states often receive international decisions rather than help shape them. He argued that geography and resources can give them advantages, but that institutions, expertise and political will are needed to use those assets when their interests are at stake.

He described sovereignty as the ability to make national rules, control resources and enforce decisions. Drawing on Morocco’s institutional experience, he also discussed Mayotte and Western Sahara, while distinguishing the two cases and stressing the need for a coherent national strategy and institutions able to sustain it.

cg.headline: Congo minister urges mindset reform to attract private investors
cg.dek: Denis Christel Sassou Nguesso says administrative conduct is driving investors to seek more favourable conditions in other countries.
paragraphs: Republic of Congo’s minister for public-private partnerships, Denis Christel Sassou Nguesso, called for changes in attitudes to improve the business climate, speaking in Brazzaville on 24 November at the 5th Vox Eco Forum. He said reform was needed in public administration, government directorates and ministerial offices.

The minister said investors facing what he described as improper conduct by officials were turning to other countries in the sub-region for more favourable conditions. He said the private sector was expected to provide nearly 70% of the funding for the new national development plan. The 2022-2026 plan had identified a financing gap of nearly 8 CFA000 billion to be filled by private investment, he said.
Sassou Nguesso said reforms were already under way but the government might not have communicated or publicised them sufficiently. He said changing conduct was now the work required.

cg.headline: L’Archer chief calls for legal, finance and business reforms in Congo
cg.dek: Gilles Tchamba says clear state rules, bolder entrepreneurs and finance that channels savings to businesses are needed for a healthier business climate.
paragraphs: Gilles Tchamba, chief executive of Congo’s Groupe L’Archer, said the business climate depends on three things: a legal framework set by the state, entrepreneurs willing to take risks and financial institutions that direct funds to businesses. He made the case in an interview at the Vox Eco Forum.

Tchamba said banks in Central Africa still rely on guarantees to approve loans, a model he said traps savings instead of moving them to borrowers. He pointed to rules from the Central African Financial Market Supervisory Commission, which have enabled crowdfunding and private-equity investment funds.

He said the financial system should provide businesses with money for investment and daily operations, while entrepreneurs also need to be willing to act. Tchamba argued that improving the business climate requires a collective response from the state, finance providers and entrepreneurs.

cg.headline: Congo opens Bacongo school built by state oil company for 9 150 pupils
cg.dek: The complex has 85 equipped classrooms and places for preschool, primary, middle and high-school pupils.
paragraphs: President Denis Sassou N’Guesso inaugurated the Complexe scolaire de l’Amitié, a public school in Bacongo, Brazzaville, on 26 November. The Société nationale des pétroles du Congo (SNPC), the state oil company, built the school, which can accommodate up to 9 150 pupils.

The school covers two hectares and has 85 equipped classrooms in about 20 buildings, Journal de Brazza reported. Its capacity is divided among 150 preschool places, 3 200 primary places, 3 800 middle-school places and 2 000 high-school places. Facilities include a science laboratory, a media library, sports grounds, a police post and 13 staff homes.

The complex is SNPC’s sixth public general-education school built across the country. Its previous projects include the Angola libre school in Makélékélé, which began operating a month and a half before the Bacongo inauguration.

ci.headline: Ivorian minister urges study of ratings body for social-security funds
ci.dek: Adama Kamara proposed assessing whether CIPRES could rate member funds, helping them build financial credibility and secure financing.
paragraphs: Ivory Coast’s social-protection minister, Adama Kamara, has called for a study of whether the Inter-African Conference on Social Welfare (CIPRES) could become a financial ratings body for social-security institutions. He made the proposal at the close of a five-day training seminar in Abidjan on 27 November.

Kamara said ratings could strengthen the institutions’ financial credibility and help them obtain resources to contribute to member states’ economies. He also urged stronger training for their managers in financial management and investment. The seminar, locally led by the state pension fund, brought together 119 officials from 14 of CIPRES’s 18 member states.

Participants studied a revised accounting plan, management indicators and prudential ratios, as well as practical requirements for implementing the tools and introducing funded pension schemes. Kamara said Ivory Coast was willing to share its experience with other member states.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast's private hospital group and ISPA plan a medical school in Abidjan
ci.dek: The CFA1.8 billion project needs ministry approval before it can open for 2027-2028 or collect tuition from students.
paragraphs: The Polyclinique internationale Sainte Anne-Marie (PISAM), a private hospital, and ISPA, a polytechnic university, signed an agreement in Abidjan on 26 November to create a private medical school, with an investment estimated at CFA1.8 billion. The fund Africa Capital International is supporting the project.

The school, called the École de médecine et d’innovation en sciences de santé d’Abidjan (EMISSA), would train students in general medicine, dental surgery and pharmacy. ISPA would oversee the theoretical teaching on its Cocody campus, while PISAM would provide hospital facilities for practical work and clinical placements. A representative of the higher education ministry confirmed receipt of the project file, which will be passed up for review.

The promoters are aiming to open in the 2027-2028 academic year, subject to ministry approval. They have not yet set tuition fees or the size of the first intake, which depends on ministry placement decisions.

ci.headline: Korhogo prosecutor warns police over detainees’ rights
ci.dek: Souleymane Koné said officers must respect legal custody limits and detainees’ rights to a lawyer, a doctor and contact with a relative.
paragraphs: Souleymane Koné, the prosecutor general at the Korhogo Court of Appeal in northern Côte d’Ivoire, urged judicial police officers to respect the rights of people in custody at the court’s 2026-2027 judicial opening on Friday, 27 November. He said detention must be justified by an investigation and authorised under the law, with judicial oversight.

Ordinary custody is limited to 48 hours and can be extended once with the public prosecutor’s authorisation, Koné said. Special laws allow up to 96 hours, also renewable once. Detainees are entitled to know the allegations, notify a relative, see a doctor and consult a lawyer. Koné said officers responsible for exceeding time limits or violating rights face civil, disciplinary and criminal sanctions.

The general prosecutor’s office handled 612 files in the 2025-2026 judicial year, including 202 correctional cases and 221 cases before the investigating chamber. Two magistrates and three court clerks took the oath at the ceremony.

eg.headline: Egypt and Sudan reaffirm 1959 Nile water rights and oppose unilateral dams
eg.dek: After talks in Cairo, the governments called on Ethiopia to return to consultation and consensus over its Eastern Nile dam project.
paragraphs: Egypt and Sudan reaffirmed their rights to Nile water under the 1959 agreement and rejected unilateral moves over Ethiopia’s dam project in the Eastern Nile basin. The position followed a Tuesday visit to Cairo by Sudanese Prime Minister Kamil Al-Tayeb Idris, who met President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and delivered a message from Sudanese Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan.

In a joint statement, the governments said unilateral steps breached international law and posed an ongoing hazard to downstream states. They urged Ethiopia to resume cooperation based on prior notification, consultation, consensus and avoiding significant harm. The two countries also agreed to track recommendations from the Permanent Joint Technical Commission for Nile Waters and hold joint meetings of their foreign and irrigation ministers.

Egypt and Sudan backed the Nile Basin Initiative and called for consultations to conclude on an inclusive basin-wide commission. They also praised a Uganda-chaired committee’s report urging changes to the framework agreement so all stakeholders’ concerns are addressed.

eg.headline: Egypt warns of rain, fog and rough Mediterranean conditions from Monday
eg.dek: The meteorological authority forecasts temperatures falling by up to 6°C, with rain of varying intensity in parts of northern Egypt.
paragraphs: Egypt’s meteorological authority warned that a low-pressure system will bring changing weather to parts of the country from Monday, November 30, with temperatures dropping by up to 6°C and rain expected. Forecasts for November 28 to December 2 put daytime conditions at mild autumn levels across most regions, but hot in Southern Upper Egypt, with cool to cold nights and early mornings.

The authority forecast fog from 4 a.m. to 9 a.m. on roads in northern Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Suez Canal cities, Central Sinai and Northern Upper Egypt; it could become dense on some routes. Light rain has an approximate 40% chance on Sunday in parts of the Northern Coasts, Northern Nile Delta, Red Sea mountain range, South Sinai and Gulf of Aqaba. From Monday, rain of varying intensity and active winds are forecast in parts of northern Egypt, with maritime navigation disrupted along sections of the Mediterranean coast.
Greater Cairo and the Nile Delta are forecast to reach 25°C on Sunday, then 22°C on Tuesday and Wednesday; lows are expected to fall from 16°C to 14°C over those days.

eg.headline: Egypt holds 21-year-old driver over Ring Road tanker crash
eg.dek: Prosecutors ordered pretrial detention and drug testing after a fuel tanker collision and fire killed 31 people in Al-Warraq.
paragraphs: Egypt's Public Prosecution ordered a 21-year-old driver held in pretrial detention pending investigations into a fuel tanker collision and fire on the Ring Road in the Al-Warraq area, which killed 31 people. The order followed his interrogation, the prosecution said in a statement on Thursday evening.

The prosecution referred him to the Forensic Medicine Authority for blood sampling and toxicology testing to determine whether he was under the influence of narcotics at the time of the crash. The authority was also ordered to collect DNA samples from the families of the dead and run matching tests to identify remains that could not otherwise be recognised. The prosecution said it had finished questioning injured victims whose health allowed.

The suspect was arrested earlier on Thursday after admitting, according to the prosecution, that he was driving at 110 kilometres per hour and weaving between lanes before hitting the rear of the tanker. The impact caused a tyre to blow out and sent the tanker off course, and the prosecution said the crash set several surrounding vehicles on fire, damaging at least 27 of them.

eg.headline: Egypt logs 102,231 traffic violations in 24 hours
eg.dek: The Interior Ministry says 42 of 997 drivers screened in nationwide campaigns tested positive for drugs, and legal action has been taken.
paragraphs: Egypt’s Interior Ministry recorded 102,231 traffic violations in 24 hours during nationwide road inspections, the ministry said. Offences included driving without valid licences, speeding, illegal parking, using mobile phones while driving and licensing breaches.

Authorities screened 997 drivers for drug use, with 42 testing positive. Separate checks in construction zones along the Regional Ring Road recorded 433 violations, including unauthorised passenger transport and failures to meet vehicle safety standards; six of 151 drivers screened there tested positive. The ministry said legal action had been taken over the offences.

Authorities also apprehended seven people subject to 11 court rulings and impounded one vehicle. Similar campaigns have run throughout November; on 9 November, the ministry reported 104,292 violations and 45 positive results among 1,094 drivers tested.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea prioritises household power as Malabo turbine repair drags on
gq.dek: The vice-president ordered the state electricity company, Sociedad de Electricidad de Guinea Ecuatorial (SEGESA), to favour homes over street lighting while a damaged turbine is.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's Vice-President Nguema Obiang Mangue has ordered the state electricity company, the Sociedad de Electricidad de Guinea Ecuatorial (SEGESA), to give household use priority over street lighting as it manages available power amid outages in several Malabo neighbourhoods. The order followed a meeting on service recovery and maintenance of electricity infrastructure.

A representative of CMEC, the company responsible for operating the Turbogas plant, said one turbine failed on 12 November and specialists estimate repairs will take three to four months. Obiang Mangue also ordered the appointment of an operations director to oversee street-light maintenance and respond to faults.

SEGESA is to prepare a technical study with CMEC and SINOHYDRO on expanding the street-lighting network. A feasibility analysis will also examine remote controls for lighting in the country's main cities; any system remains subject to the study's findings.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea lawmakers demand explanation of monthly social-housing charge
gq.dek: The government's public works minister told parliament the levy is a hard social problem, while deputies pressed for an account of where the money goes.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's Chamber of Deputies summoned government ministers to explain the monthly deduction of CFA10,000 from residents of social housing across the country, a complaint that has caused widespread unrest. Deputies want to know where the money goes and how it is used.

Justino Nchama Ondo, the delegate minister for public works, territorial planning and housing, appeared on behalf of the government and said the issue was a social problem that was hard for the government to solve. He asked parliament for support in finding a lasting solution. Deputies said the housing developments were not receiving maintenance and that the current balance of the account had not been justified.

Deputies recommended that each resident's deduction be credited to their monthly housing repayment and that neighbourhood communities organise cleaning of their estates. Salvador Nguema Mangue, spokesman for the Democratic Coalition, demanded an official government explanation, while José Pablo Nvo Owono Aviri, deputy spokesman for the ruling Democratic Party of Equatorial Guinea (PDGE), also backed using the money to pay off the housing.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea hands regional presidency to Chad
gq.dek: Chad will lead the Central African Economic Community’s work, with security, economic cooperation and regional institutions on its agenda.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea’s President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo transferred the rotating presidency of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS) to Chad, ending Equatorial Guinea’s term at the head of the regional organisation.

Obiang said his mandate had made progress on peace, security and integration, while Chad’s president thanked member states for their confidence. Chad’s new presidency will direct the organisation’s work during the coming period, with security cooperation, economic ties and stronger community institutions among its agenda items.

The handover continues the organisation’s system of rotating leadership among its members. Chad’s president said he would continue efforts to promote stability, integration and economic development in Central Africa.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea holds HIV testing and aid events in Malabo and Bata
gq.dek: The Saturday programme combines public testing and prevention talks with donations for people living with HIV who face financial hardship.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea’s health ministry is holding public HIV awareness and testing events in Malabo and Bata on Saturday, 28 November, alongside activities for World AIDS Day. The programme will run simultaneously in both cities and is open to the public.

Organisers said activities include prevention talks, condom and information-material distribution, a public fun run and a group zumba session. The events will also collect voluntary cash contributions and non-perishable food for people living with HIV who are facing economic hardship. The education ministry, BANGE Business School, the Constancia Mangue Nsue Okomo Foundation and non-governmental organisations are collaborating.
The programme invites young people, families, public and private institutions, businesses and civil-society groups to take part.

gq.headline: Cuba seeks to restart health fairs in remote Equatorial Guinea
gq.dek: The Cuban ambassador says the events would bring specialist care and early disease detection to isolated communities.
paragraphs: Cuba wants to restart health fairs in remote parts of Equatorial Guinea, bringing medical care to communities that are difficult to reach. The plan is intended to detect illnesses early through consultations, tests and medical check-ups.

Cuban ambassador Ángel Gustavo Suárez Cordero said the fairs would be organised with the country’s health and interior ministries and regional authorities. He said they would bring specialist care to people in isolated areas who need it most.

er.headline: Abiy says Eritrea rejected power, road and port offers as tensions grow
er.dek: Ethiopia's prime minister accuses Asmara of arming forces hostile to Ethiopia and warns that destruction will fall upon Eritrea if it does not change course.
paragraphs: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed accused Eritrea of arming forces hostile to Ethiopia and warned of grave consequences if Asmara did not change course. Speaking to parliament on November 26, he set two conditions for peaceful coexistence: that Eritrea stop arming and collaborating with those forces, and that it join joint development, with Ethiopia contributing the ideas, the money and the labour.

The state-run Ethiopian News Agency reported that Ethiopia had offered Eritrea electricity at Ethiopian domestic tariffs and proposed joint road and port projects, and that Eritrea had rejected the initiatives. Abiy said relations deteriorated after Eritrean forces entered Tigray during the 2020-22 war, accusing them of killing young people, destroying infrastructure and looting property.

Eight days earlier, Reuters reported that the two sides had massed forces along their shared border, bringing the armies within striking distance of each other. Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel dismissed the reports as propaganda.

ke.headline: Kiambu court order halts 72 million litres of daily water supply
ke.dek: The county government obtained interim orders barring Kenya's national water agency from supplying six providers that serve homes and businesses.
paragraphs: Kenya's national bulk water agency, the Athi Water Works Development Agency (AWWDA), has stopped bulk water deliveries to six water service providers in Kiambu County after a High Court order barred direct supply. The shutdown affects about 72 million litres a day, the agency said in a Friday statement.

The Kiambu High Court issued interim orders on November 18, 2026, after the Kiambu county government applied to stop the deliveries. AWWDA chief executive Joseph Kamau said the agency had complied and would pursue lawful options to resolve the dispute. The six providers distribute water to households, businesses and institutions.

Ruiru-Juja Water and Sewerage Company receives 47.5 million litres daily, while the other five providers receive between one million and 10 million litres each. The agency did not set an end date for the shutdown or specify alternative supply arrangements.

ke.headline: Kenya's savings co-operatives face money-laundering gaps as grey-list exit effort conti...
ke.dek: Financial sector experts say weak monitoring, member checks and reporting systems leave the societies exposed to abuse and short of compliance capacity.
paragraphs: Kenyan savings and credit co-operative societies (SACCOs), member-owned lenders, face gaps in transaction monitoring, member verification and reporting of suspicious activity as the country seeks removal from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the intergovernmental body that sets anti-money-laundering standards, from its grey list. Financial sector experts raised the concerns at a Nairobi forum on SACCO compliance and digital payments organised by Innovative Software Technologies Limited.

Zachariah Obari, compliance director at ABC Bank, said many SACCOs still need the technology and trained staff to spot unusual transactions and report them to authorities. He called for capacity building, led by the Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (SASRA), the state regulator, working with SACCO leaders, and said written policies alone were not enough to meet anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism financing obligations.

The forum brought SACCO representatives and financial-sector participants together to discuss regulatory duties and technology-based responses. Obari said failure to improve safeguards could undermine Kenya's campaign to address deficiencies identified by international financial-crime watchdogs.

za.headline: Johannesburg raises residential water tariffs from Tuesday 1 December
za.dek: The new Level 2 rates lift the monthly water charge for a household using 10 kilolitres from R134.28 to R196.72, excluding other charges.
paragraphs: The City of Johannesburg will raise stepped water tariffs for residential accounts from Tuesday, 1 December, under Level 2 restrictions introduced to protect the municipality's water supply system and prevent reservoir depletion. The changes apply to household and multi-dwelling accounts, while commercial and industrial tariffs are excluded.

The City says a household using 10 kilolitres a month will pay R196.72 for water, up R62.44 from the normal R134.28, before VAT and other charges. The first six kilolitres, previously charged at R0.00 per kilolitre, will cost R7.80 per kilolitre. Registered indigent and Expanded Social Package households retain approved Free Basic Water relief.

The City says it is consuming 1 709 million litres of water a day against a bulk supply allocation of 1 524 million litres, an excess of roughly 185 million litres daily. Deemed-consumption and prepaid customers are not subject to the stepped tariff adjustment; those areas will instead receive a 20% flow reduction on zone supply meters.

za.headline: Mashaba returns as Johannesburg mayor, beating the DA's Helen Zille
za.dek: The ActionSA leader was elected at a council sitting, after coalition talks involving the ANC, ActionSA and the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) party.
paragraphs: Herman Mashaba has returned as executive mayor of the City of Johannesburg, after councillors elected him at a council sitting in the Johannesburg Council Chamber on Friday, 27 November. He beat Helen Zille of the Democratic Alliance (DA), the party he served under as mayor from 2016 to 2019. He now leads ActionSA.

Councillors voted after reports of a coalition agreement involving the African National Congress (ANC), ActionSA and the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF). The DA won the most seats in the 4 November local government elections, with 91 of the 270 seats, followed by the ANC with 63 and ActionSA with 43, but it fell short of an outright majority.
Zille had said that last-minute coalition negotiations were still underway ahead of the vote, and she declined to say whether the DA was negotiating with ActionSA.

za.headline: Water commission portal targets municipal losses as non-revenue water hits 47.4%
za.dek: The resource hub includes field-tested tools, while a planned sharing feature would let councils pass on approaches that worked in their networks.
paragraphs: The Water Research Commission is developing a portal to help South African municipalities tackle non-revenue water, which the department’s national water balance puts at 47.4%. The commission identified 84 resources for the hub, research psychologist Leonie Vorster said at a webinar in Durban on 25 November.

Vorster said the next phase would let registered users share approaches that had worked in their networks. The portal has been in development for about two years, and some municipalities have started using it. It will bring together guidelines, tools and information on technologies tested in the field, water specialist Dr Manjusha Sunil said.

The national water balance, drawing on the department’s 2023 No Drop assessment, estimated water losses at 40.8%. Non-revenue water also includes supplies that generate no revenue; officials need to distinguish leaks, which require repairs, from inaccurate readings or billing errors.

za.headline: Cape Town terminal deploys 14 spreaders for fruit exports
za.dek: Transnet Port Terminals says the R83 million equipment purchase is intended to reduce crane stoppages during vessel loading.
paragraphs: The Cape Town Container Terminal has invested R83 million (US$4.78 million) in 14 container spreaders as South Africa’s deciduous fruit export season begins. Transnet Port Terminals said the equipment is being deployed across ship-to-shore, rail-mounted gantry and mobile harbour cranes.

Terminal manager Noxolo Thabatha said the spreaders’ hydraulic twist-locks secure containers and are intended to reduce mechanical delays during vessel loading. Four units will serve the Cape Town Multi-Purpose Terminal, which supports the container terminal during peak export periods.

At the container terminal, ship working hours improved 15% in the financial year ended March 2026, while truck turnaround fell from 52 minutes to 35 minutes. Strong south-easterly winds cost the terminal 79 operating days last year; during weather stoppages, the two terminals will use the Belcon inland facility to stage landside movements and receive refrigerated containers.

ng.headline: Nigeria targets 1.4 million tonnes of milk a year within five years
ng.dek: The livestock minister also set out a potential $3.2 billion beef export market, saying the figure represents an opportunity, not current earnings.
paragraphs: Nigeria’s Federal Government has set a five-year target to raise annual domestic milk production to 1.4 million metric tonnes and develop a potential $3.2 billion beef export market. Livestock Development Minister Muktar Maina announced the goals in Lagos at the Second National Council on Livestock Development.

Maina said the export figure describes a market opportunity, not existing revenue. He proposed a national framework for animal identification, traceability, disease reporting and meat certification, supported by a central data platform. In Lagos, more than 90% of the 2.9 million cattle consumed annually are processed at the Oko-Oba open slabs, he said.

The government is expanding annual vaccine production capacity at the National Veterinary Research Institute from 120 million to 850 million doses. Maina also said 21 states had livestock agencies and 30 were taking part in a World Bank-assisted livestock project.

ng.headline: AGRA and SMEDAN target $25m for agricultural SMEs
ng.dek: The partners also launched a cost-sharing facility, seeded with $100,000 by AGRA, to make professional business services more affordable.
paragraphs: The Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) and Nigeria’s Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) are targeting at least $25m in financing for agricultural small and medium-sized enterprises. They also unveiled a facility to help businesses afford professional support services at a meeting in Ibadan, Oyo State.

AGRA has committed an initial $100,000 to the Multi-Donor Business Development Services Cost-Sharing Facility, which will pool contributions from development partners, financial institutions and government agencies. Dr Godswill Aguiyi, representing AGRA Nigeria Country Director Rufus Idris, said weak financial records, corporate governance, technology use and market intelligence made it harder for agribusinesses to attract investors.

The broader project also seeks to connect businesses with buyers and financial institutions. The initiative aims to expand opportunities for women and young people in agriculture; AGRA said its recent Youth in Agribusiness Innovation Contest drew more than 10,000 applications, and 10 selected entrepreneurs received a combined N17m in cash awards.

The Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) and Nigeria’s Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) are targeting at least $25m in financing for agricultural small and medium-sized enterprises. They also unveiled a facility to help businesses afford professional support services at a meeting in Ibadan, Oyo State.

AGRA has committed an initial $100,000 to the Multi-Donor Business Development Services Cost-Sharing Facility, which will pool contributions from development partners, financial institutions and government agencies. et.headline: African Union and China train officials in AI-based disaster warnings
et.dek: A five-day Addis Ababa workshop taught participants to use AI, satellite data and geographic information systems to improve hazard forecasting.
paragraphs: The African Union Commission and China trained officials in Addis Ababa from November 23 to 27 on using artificial intelligence, geographic information systems and other tools in multi-hazard early warning systems. The five-day workshop at African Union headquarters brought together participants from member states, regional economic communities and continental institutions.

The training covered satellite observation, remote sensing and data analysis for monitoring hazards, assessing vulnerability and forecasting impacts. Participants were expected to apply products from the Africa Multi-Hazard Early Warning and Early Action System in national disaster planning. African Union Commissioner Moses Vilakati said the 2026/2027 El Nino threatens up to 50 million people with hunger.

The African Union says floods, droughts, tropical cyclones and heatwaves cause human, environmental and economic losses, while limited institutional capacity and warning coverage constrain preparedness. China's deputy mission head Zhang Wei said only about 40% of African countries have established multi-hazard warning systems.

et.headline: Ethiopia and AAMFI sign deal to host permanent secretariat in Addis Ababa
et.dek: The Host Country Agreement, signed at the Foreign Ministry, sets the framework for the Alliance's permanent base and closer coordination with the African Union.
paragraphs: The Alliance of African Multilateral Financial Institutions (AAMFI), also known as the Africa Club, and the Government of Ethiopia have signed a Host Country Agreement to establish the Alliance's permanent Secretariat in Addis Ababa. The agreement was signed at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs by Ambassador Hadera, State Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Corneille Karekezi, chairperson of the AAMFI Governing Council and group managing director and chief executive of the African Reinsurance Corporation (Africa Re).

Ambassador Hadera said the agreement was an important step in strengthening cooperation between Ethiopia and AAMFI. He pointed to Addis Ababa's position as the seat of the African Union and numerous international organisations, and to Ethiopian Airlines' international connections, as advantages for the Alliance's continental and global work. Dr Karekezi said the Secretariat would help members work together, mobilise African capital and advance an African-led financial architecture.

The Secretariat will give the Alliance an institutional base to deepen collaboration among its members and with continental partners, and to pursue joint initiatives on Africa's development financing. The Alliance was launched in Addis Ababa on 17 February 2024 with the African Union Commission and brings together African-owned and African-controlled multilateral financial institutions.

gh.headline: Civil society groups reject Ghana's five-year presidential term proposal
gh.dek: More than 100 groups also want citizens to elect local leaders without presidential shortlisting in the proposed metropolitan, municipal and district chief executive system.
paragraphs: More than 100 civil society organisations in Ghana rejected a proposal to extend presidential and parliamentary terms from four years to five, and called for changes to plans for electing Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), the heads of local government. They said citizens should choose local-government leaders without presidential interference.

The groups made their positions during a two-day engagement with the Constitutional Reform Implementation Committee, which is seeking agreement on proposed amendments to Ghana's 1992 Constitution. Committee Executive Secretary Oliver Barker-Vormawor said the organisations agreed with about 89% of the government's proposals, while outstanding issues fell from 41 to 10.

Koku Anyidoho, an adviser to the Christian Council of Ghana's General Secretary, said 18 position papers were presented. Barker-Vormawor said the unresolved proposals, including term length and whether MPs should be ministers, would go to Cabinet for possible reconsideration.

gh.headline: Kuapa Kokoo warns illegal mining and erratic weather are cutting cocoa output
gh.dek: Managing Director Emmanuel Kwabena Arthur says pods are scarce at the harvest peak, while polluted rivers leave farmers without clean water.
paragraphs: Ghana’s cocoa production is unusually low at the peak of the season, Kuapa Kokoo Managing Director Emmanuel Kwabena Arthur said at the farmers’ 32nd annual delegates conference. He said the pods on trees were not encouraging as the season approached the end of November.

Arthur said illegal miners, known locally as galamsey, have taken over abandoned cocoa farms and polluted rivers. Farmers lack clean water to irrigate crops and mix pesticides and insecticides, he said. Changing rainfall patterns have also disrupted flowering and pod formation and made planting and farm-maintenance schedules harder to predict.

Ghana Cocoa Board has projected lower production this year than last year, Arthur said, but he warned output could fall further below expectations. He urged the government to strengthen enforcement against illegal mining and chainsaw operations in forest reserves and cocoa-growing communities.

gh.headline: CSIR finds climate resilience gap in Ghana’s Feed Ghana Programme
gh.dek: The assessment says the programme is not aligned with the climate-resilience pillar of the African agriculture strategy as sector policy is revised.
paragraphs: Ghana’s Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) found that the Feed Ghana Programme is not aligned with the climate-resilience pillar of the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme’s Kampala Strategy. The assessment was conducted by CSIR’s Science and Technology Policy Research Institute as the government revises its Food and Agriculture Sector Development Policy.

Researcher Justina Onumah said the programme has production targets but needs greater attention to climate resilience. Her team put forward four options: revise the sector policy while keeping Feed Ghana, align the programme directly with the continental framework, revise both together, or make no immediate changes. The options were assessed for policy coherence, feasibility and timing, programme continuity and cost.
The sector policy dates to 2008. CSIR’s research institute is on the technical committee for the new policy and is expected to contribute evidence, Onumah said.

gh.headline: GMet forecasts 39°C heat in Bolgatanga and Nalerigu
gh.dek: The weather service also expects late-afternoon rain or thunderstorms in parts of the coast and forest belt.
paragraphs: Ghana’s Meteorological Agency (GMet) forecasts afternoon temperatures of 39°C in Bolgatanga and Nalerigu on Saturday. Tamale, Wa and Jirapa are expected to reach 38°C under dry, hazy skies.

GMet forecasts sunny periods and cloud build-up across southern Ghana, followed by possible rain or thunderstorms in some coastal and forest-belt areas late in the afternoon and evening. The agency also expects a 60% chance of fog in Akim Oda and Sunyani, with mist across 18 other coastal, forest and upland stations, including Bole. It advises drivers to watch for reduced visibility early in the day.

Koforidua and Akim Oda are forecast to reach 34°C, with the chance of thunderstorms rising from 30% in the afternoon to 40% in the evening. Kumasi, Obuasi and Kwahu Tafo are expected to reach 33°C before a 40% evening storm chance.

gh.headline: Westerwelle Foundation opens Accra hub for more than 180 members
gh.dek: The German organisation plans at least three more African start-up hubs within five years after opening its fifth facility on the continent.
paragraphs: The Westerwelle Foundation, a German organisation that supports young entrepreneurs, opened its fifth African start-up hub in Accra. The facility is expected to accommodate more than 180 members, and the foundation plans to establish at least three more hubs in Africa within five years.

Managing Director Paul Steffens said the foundation had supported more than 2,400 entrepreneurs and helped create over 1,200 jobs through its African activities. Ghana Country Director Alhassan Baba Muniru said the Accra hub would offer workspace, training rooms, private offices and networking. Selected entrepreneurs could receive funded incubation, including six months of training, mentorship and workspace; initial programmes will focus on digital and green innovation and the creative economy.

Germany’s development ministry representative Bärbel Kofler cited a programme offering eligible young businesses grants of up to €100,000, provided they mobilise equivalent funding from other investors. The foundation said it would continue working with government agencies, investors and business organisations.

cd.headline: Congo health division urges proper medicine use amid resistance deaths
cd.dek: Data from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), a US-based research group, link antimicrobial resistance to about 65 200 deaths a year in the Democratic.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo's division for combating antimicrobial resistance called on health workers and the public to use medicines properly, at a conference at the University of Kinshasa on 25 November. Data from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) associate resistance with about 65 200 deaths each year in the country.

The division's head, Dr. Aurélie Mambu Nsimba, told Radio Okapi that people should follow prescriptions and recommended doses. She said patients should not take antibiotics without a health worker's prescription and should complete the treatment. Children under five are among the groups most vulnerable to antimicrobial resistance.

A student at the university, identified as Claudine, pointed to self-medication and excessive antibiotic use, and called for wider public awareness. The conference was held alongside World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed from 18 to 24 November.

cd.headline: Congo and Uganda agree to settle security row through diplomacy
cd.dek: Kinshasa had summoned Uganda's mission chief after posts by Uganda's army chief about eastern Congo, and Uganda has announced it will withdraw troops from Lubero.
paragraphs: Congo's foreign minister, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, spoke by phone on Friday, 27 November, with her Ugandan counterpart, Adonia Ayebare. According to the Congolese foreign ministry, they discussed recent public statements on regional and bilateral security, and agreed to handle such issues through official and diplomatic channels.

The call followed Kinshasa's summoning, on 24 November, of the head of Uganda's embassy mission in Kinshasa. The ministry said that move came after posts on X by Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba about the security situation in eastern Congo, some of which showed support for the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, a political movement led by former president Joseph Kabila. Kinshasa had asked Ugandan authorities for explanations.

The ministers reaffirmed respect for each country's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and said they would strengthen cooperation in defence, the economy and public health. Uganda has also announced the coming withdrawal of its troops from Lubero, in North Kivu, where they have been deployed since January 2025 alongside Congolese forces against the Allied Democratic Forces.

cd.headline: Tshisekedi to press central African summit on UN resolution 2773
cd.dek: The DR Congo president arrived in Malabo on Friday 27 November for the 27th summit of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), the regional bloc.
paragraphs: DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi arrived in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea, on Friday 27 November for the 27th summit of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), the regional bloc. The Congolese presidency said he intends to seek full implementation of United Nations Security Council resolution 2773, concerning security in eastern DR Congo.

Adopted in February 2025, the resolution calls on the Rwandan Defence Forces to stop supporting M23 and withdraw immediately and without preconditions from Congolese territory. It also demands that rebels of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), which replaced the former AFC/M23 coalition, leave areas they control in DR Congo.
The summit is also set to discuss ECCAS's Vision 2050, its 2026-2030 strategic plan and funding mechanisms, as well as energy, health, maritime security and border governance.
